title: Left Bousfield model structures and their fibrant objects
statement:
Use the universe and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the model and simplicial-model terminology of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a left proper combinatorial simplicial model category. Left proper means stability of weak equivalences under pushout along cofibrations, and combinatorial means locally presentable with small sets generating its two model weak factorization systems; locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for some regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve these colimits. Let $T$ be a small set of cofibrations between cofibrant objects of $\mathcal M$. For fibrant $Z$, call it $T$-local if every $(A\to B)\in T$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(B,Z)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Z)$. A map $f:X\to Y$ is a $T$-equivalence if $\operatorname{Map}^h(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$ is an equivalence for every such fibrant local $Z$, where $\operatorname{Map}^h$ uses cofibrant and fibrant replacements in $\mathcal M$.

There exists a left proper combinatorial simplicial model structure $L_T\mathcal M$ on the same underlying category, with the same simplicial enrichment, tensors and cotensors. Its cofibrations are those of $\mathcal M$ and its weak equivalences are exactly the $T$-equivalences. Its fibrant objects are precisely the fibrant $T$-local objects of $\mathcal M$, and it admits functorial factorizations. The identity adjunction $\mathcal M\rightleftarrows L_T\mathcal M$ is Quillen with identity as the left Quillen functor from $\mathcal M$. No infinity-categorical identification of the localized model with a local presheaf subcategory is part of this assertion.

source.place: Proposition A.3.7.3 (printed pp. 908-910), restricted to a small set of cofibrations between cofibrant objects; its proof constructs functorial local fibrant replacement. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: Write $C$ for the old cofibrations, $W_0$ for the old weak equivalences, $\mathcal Z$ for the old fibrant $T$-local objects, and $W$ for the stated $T$-equivalences. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], $\operatorname{Map}^h$ is a mapping space in the old localization, so it sends $W_0$ to equivalences in either variable. Hence $W_0\subseteq W$, $\mathcal Z$ is closed under old weak equivalences between fibrant objects, and $W$ is closed under arrow retracts and has two-out-of-three: apply each functor $\operatorname{Map}^h(-,Z)$ and these properties of equivalences of spaces. The enriched and derived tests agree for the cofibrant endpoints of $T$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; identify local tests and elementary closure properties of W Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: For a cofibration $i$, [lem-coef-cofibration-local-mapping-test] identifies $i\in W$ with trivial fibrancy of every $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(i,Z)$, $Z\in\mathcal Z$, even when the source of $i$ is not cofibrant. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] this is equivalent, by tensor/cotensor adjunction, to $i$ having the left lifting property against every $Z^{\Delta^n}\to Z^{\partial\Delta^n}$. Since $C$ itself is a left lifting class, $C\cap W$ is the intersection of two left lifting classes. Retract and pushout closure follow from [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. For a transfinite composite, construct a lift successively at each successor stage; at a limit stage its compatible earlier lifts give the required map by the colimit universal property. Thus this intersection is weakly saturated, including coproducts (attach the summands in a well-order).

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; verify weak saturation of the new trivial cofibrations Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: Choose a small old generating set $J$ of trivial cofibrations. For $t:A\to B$ in $T$ and $n\geq0$ put $t\mathbin\square\partial_n:(A\otimes\Delta^n)\amalg_{A\otimes\partial\Delta^n}(B\otimes\partial\Delta^n)\to B\otimes\Delta^n$ and set $S=J\cup\{t\mathbin\square\partial_n\}$. This is small, and all its members are old cofibrations by the old simplicial axiom. Each $t\mathbin\square\partial_n$ lies in $W$: for $Z\in\mathcal Z$, $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(t,Z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration, and its Leibniz mapping map against $\partial_n$ is again a trivial Kan fibration. Indeed lifting a boundary against that map is lifting against the Cartesian pushout-product of two boundary inclusions; this is degreewise injective, so the lift exists by the Kan model weak factorization system. Apply the local cofibration test to conclude. Also $J\subseteq W_0\subseteq W$. Finally $Z\to1$ lifts against $S$ exactly when it lifts against $J$ and all $t\mathbin\square\partial_n$: the first means old fibrant, and the second means $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(t,Z)$ has all boundary lifts, or equivalently $T$-local. Thus $S$-injective objects are exactly $\mathcal Z$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; choose a small set imposing the local fibrant extension conditions Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] to $S$ and $X\to1$. It gives a functor $R$ and a natural $\eta_X:X\to RX$ with $RX\in\mathcal Z$ and $\eta_X$ in the weak saturation of $S$. Step 2 and $S\subseteq C\cap W$ give $\eta_X\in C\cap W$. The functor $R$ preserves sufficiently filtered colimits: the factorization middle-object functor does, and $X\mapsto(X\to1)$ preserves such colimits because every nonempty filtered index is connected, so the colimit of its constant terminal diagram is terminal. Consequently, by naturality of $\eta$ and two-out-of-three, $f\in W$ if and only if $Rf\in W$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; accessible local fibrant replacement, properties (i)-(iii) in HTT Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: For $u:U\to V$ between objects of $\mathcal Z$, $u\in W$ implies that precomposition by $u$ is bijective on $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}^h(-,U)$ and on $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}^h(-,V)$. Surjectivity for $U$ gives $g:V\to U$ in the old homotopy category with $gu=1_U$. Injectivity for $V$, applied to $(ug)u=u=1_Vu$, gives $ug=1_V$. Thus $u$ is invertible in the old homotopy category and is in $W_0$ by [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences]. The converse follows from $W_0\subseteq W$. Step 4 therefore proves $f\in W\Longleftrightarrow Rf\in W_0$. By [lem-coef-model-weak-equivalences-accessible] the old weak-equivalence arrows form a replete accessible subcategory. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-arrow-inverse-image] to $R:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ to conclude that $W$ is a replete accessible subcategory of the arrow category.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; identify W as an accessible inverse image without presuming localization existence Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the original small generating cofibrations. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] to factor any $c:X\to Y$ in $C$ as $p a$, with $a:X\to E$ in the weak saturation of $I$ and $p\in I^{\square}$, an old trivial fibration. Lifting $c$ against $p$ in the square with top $a$ and bottom $1_Y$ gives $h:Y\to E$ with $hc=a$ and $ph=1_Y$. The arrow maps $(1_X,h):c\to a$ and $(1_X,p):a\to c$ exhibit $c$ as a retract of $a$. Conversely the weak saturation of $I$ lies in $C$ because $C$ is a left lifting class, whose transfinite closure was checked in step 2. Thus $I$ generates $C$ weakly. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-smith-model-recognition] now hold: the underlying category is complete and locally presentable by assumption, $C$ is small-generated, step 2 gives saturation of $C\cap W$, step 5 gives accessibility, and step 1 gives two-out-of-three. An arrow in $C^{\square}$ is an old trivial fibration, hence in $W_0\subseteq W$, verifying the last hypothesis. The recognition theorem supplies a combinatorial model structure with precisely $C,W$, fibrations $(C\cap W)^{\square}$, and functorial factorizations. Denote it $L_T\mathcal M$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; check every hypothesis of Smith recognition Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: The old simplicial enrichment, tensors and cotensors satisfy the new pushout-product axiom. If $i\in C$ and $j$ is a simplicial-set monomorphism, $i\mathbin\square j$ is in $C$ by the old simplicial axiom. If $j$ is also a weak equivalence, the OLD simplicial axiom makes $i\mathbin\square j$ an old trivial cofibration, hence a member of $W$. If instead $i\in C\cap W$, the local cofibration test gives $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(i,Z)$ trivial Kan for every $Z\in\mathcal Z$. Under adjunction, $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(i\mathbin\square j,Z)$ is its Leibniz mapping map against $j$. It has the right lifting property against every boundary, since $j\mathbin\square\partial_n$ is degreewise injective (a union of subsets inside the Cartesian product), and a trivial Kan fibration lifts against all monomorphisms. The local test implies $i\mathbin\square j\in C\cap W$. These two triviality assertions and the lifting adjunction give exactly the new mapping-space fibration axiom. The tensor unit is the same $\Delta^0$, so its identity constraint is unchanged. Thus the new model is simplicial.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; verify the same simplicial structure, with both triviality cases Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: A new fibrant $Z$ has the right lifting property against $C\cap W$, hence against $S$, and so lies in $\mathcal Z$ by step 3. Conversely, for $Z\in\mathcal Z$ the local cofibration test makes $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(i,Z)$ a trivial Kan fibration for every $i\in C\cap W$. Its boundary lift for $n=0$ gives every ordinary extension $A\to Z$ along $i:A\to B$. Hence $Z\to1$ is a new fibration. This proves precisely the fibrant-object assertion, including the case $T=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; derive both directions of the fibrant-object characterization Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: To check left properness, push out $f:X\to Y$ in $W$ along a cofibration $c:X\to X\prime$. Factor $f=p i$ using the OLD model, with $i:X\to E$ a cofibration and $p:E\to Y$ an old trivial fibration. Since $p\in W_0\subseteq W$, two-out-of-three gives $i\in C\cap W$. Put $E\prime=E\amalg_X X\prime$. Its map from $X\prime$ is in $C\cap W$ by step 2. Moreover $E\to E\prime$ is the pushout of $c$ and is an old cofibration. Old left properness applied to $p$ along THIS cofibration gives $E\prime\to Y\amalg_E E\prime$ in $W_0$. The pushout universal property identifies $Y\amalg_E E\prime$ with $Y\amalg_X X\prime$ and identifies the composite with the required pushout of $f$. Both factors lie in $W$, proving new left properness.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, supporting left Bousfield model construction; write the two successive pushout squares, rather than assuming properness Agent expansion, checked against HTT Proposition A.3.7.3 online.

proof.text: The identity is its own right adjoint, preserves $C$, and sends every old trivial cofibration into $C\cap W$ because $W_0\subseteq W$. It is therefore left Quillen from $\mathcal M$ to $L_T\mathcal M$. Steps 6-9 give every claimed property; no infinity-categorical comparison for the new model was used.
